Golden Rules (Comprehensive Rules 2.1-2.10.2, examples omitted):
2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.

2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

Golden Rules (Comprehensive Rules 2.1-2.10.2, examples omitted):
2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

How to answer:
- The rules are permissive: something is allowed unless a rule or card text forbids it or a cost can't be paid. "No rule explicitly permits it" is not a reason to answer No.

- Only a cost (text before a colon, or "pay ...") can stop an effect from being used. Effect text that can't fully happen resolves as much as possible (2.4, 10.10). "You may" parts are optional.
- Numbered sub-steps of a rule happen in their numbered order.
- When two retrieved rules seem to conflict, the more specific one wins, and card text beats the rules (2.5). Check every preloaded rule before answering, not only the first.
- If the preloaded rules don't settle it, call search_rules or get_rule before answering.

2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

Golden Rules (Comprehensive Rules 2.1-2.10.2, examples omitted):
2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

How to answer:
- The rules are permissive: something is allowed unless a rule or card text forbids it or a cost can't be paid. "No rule explicitly permits it" is not a reason to answer No.
- To judge a statement true or false, first decide whether the statement as written, including any "not" or "may not", is true; pick Yes only if it is true. State that conclusion in one line just before your final answer line.
- Only a cost (text before a colon, or "pay ...") can stop an effect from being used. Effect text that can't fully happen resolves as much as possible (2.4, 10.10). "You may" parts are optional.
- Numbered sub-steps of a rule happen in their numbered order.
- When two retrieved rules seem to conflict, the more specific one wins, and card text beats the rules (2.5). Check every preloaded rule before answering, not only the first.
- If the preloaded rules don't settle it, call search_rules or get_rule before answering.

Golden Rules (Comprehensive Rules 2.1-2.10.2, examples omitted):
2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

How to answer:
- The rules are permissive: something is allowed unless a rule or card text forbids it or a cost can't be paid. "No rule explicitly permits it" is not a reason to answer No.
- To judge a statement true or false, first decide whether the statement as written, including any "not" or "may not", is true; pick Yes only if it is true. State that conclusion in one line just before your final answer line.
- Only a cost (text before a colon, or "pay ...") can stop an effect from being used. Effect text that can't fully happen resolves as much as possible (2.4, 10.10). "You may" parts are optional.
- Numbered sub-steps of a rule happen in their numbered order.
- When two retrieved rules seem to conflict, the more specific one wins, and card text beats the rules (2.5). Check every preloaded rule before answering, not only the first.
- If the preloaded rules don't settle it, call search_rules or get_rule before answering.

Golden Rules (Comprehensive Rules 2.1-2.10.2, examples omitted):
2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

- The rules are permissive: something is allowed unless a rule or card text forbids it or a cost can't be paid. "No rule explicitly permits it" is not a reason to answer No.

- Numbered sub-steps of a rule happen in their numbered order.
- When two retrieved rules seem to conflict, the more specific one wins, and card text beats the rules (2.5). Check every preloaded rule before answering, not only the first.
- If the preloaded rules don't settle it, call search_rules or get_rule before answering.

Golden Rules (Comprehensive Rules 2.1-2.10.2, examples omitted):
2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

- The rules are permissive: something is allowed unless a rule or card text forbids it or a cost can't be paid. "No rule explicitly permits it" is not a reason to answer No.

- Numbered sub-steps of a rule happen in their numbered order.

2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.

2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.

2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.

2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

- The rules are permissive: something is allowed unless a rule or card text forbids it or a cost can't be paid. "No rule explicitly permits it" is not a reason to answer No.

2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.

- Errata override printed card text.
- Give a pasted deck list to parse_deck first. Label strategy as judgment.
- At most 6 tool calls per question. Keep the answer short.

Golden Rules (Comprehensive Rules 2.1-2.10.2, examples omitted):
2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

How to answer:
- The rules are permissive: something is allowed unless a rule or card text forbids it or a cost can't be paid. "No rule explicitly permits it" is not a reason to answer No.

- Only a cost (text before a colon, or "pay ...") can stop an effect from being used. Effect text that can't fully happen resolves as much as possible (2.4, 10.10). "You may" parts are optional.
- Numbered sub-steps of a rule happen in their numbered order.
- When two retrieved rules seem to conflict, the more specific one wins, and card text beats the rules (2.5). Check every preloaded rule before answering, not only the first.
- If the preloaded rules don't settle it, call search_rules or get_rule before answering.

Golden Rules (Comprehensive Rules 2.1-2.10.2, examples omitted):
2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

How to answer:
- The rules are permissive: something is allowed unless a rule or card text forbids it or a cost can't be paid. "No rule explicitly permits it" is not a reason to answer No.
- To judge a statement true or false, first decide whether the statement as written, including any "not" or "may not", is true; pick Yes only if it is true. State that conclusion in one line just before your final answer line.
- Only a cost (text before a colon, or "pay ...") can stop an effect from being used. Effect text that can't fully happen resolves as much as possible (2.4, 10.10). "You may" parts are optional.
- Numbered sub-steps of a rule happen in their numbered order.
- When two retrieved rules seem to conflict, the more specific one wins, and card text beats the rules (2.5). Check every preloaded rule before answering, not only the first.
- If the preloaded rules don't settle it, call search_rules or get_rule before answering.

Golden Rules (Comprehensive Rules 2.1-2.10.2, examples omitted):
2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

Warning: some terms here are the reverse of other card games. In these rules an attack spends a friendly ready Unit (rule 9.1), and a spent rival Unit is a valid attack target (rule 9.3.2.1). Where the rules text and your expectations differ, the rules text is right.

- Answer only from tool results in this conversation, including the ones looked up before you were asked.
- If no tool result is relevant, say the snapshot does not cover it. Do not guess.
- Tournament procedure, penalties, deck registration, event policy: use the Tournament Rules (TR 3.4.2), cite them. Anything in neither is not covered.
- Cite rule numbers (rule 9.3.2.1) and card slugs in backticks (`v-streetkid`).
- A card's identity is its slug; several cards share a name. If find_card says ambiguous, ask which card or answer for each.
- Errata override printed card text.
- Give a pasted deck list to parse_deck first. Label strategy as judgment.
- At most 6 tool calls per question. Keep the answer short.

Golden Rules (Comprehensive Rules 2.1-2.10.2, examples omitted):
2.1. When an effect tells you to do something, you must resolve it. See EFFECTS.
2.1.1. If an effect includes “you may,” you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect.
2.2. When you activate an effect, you must resolve it.
2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.
2.7. If an effect has a cost, you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect.
2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).
2.9. If a game mechanic makes both players do an effect at the same time. The turn player will resolve first, followed by their Rival.
2.10. A game value can be a negative number.
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

How to answer:
- The rules are permissive: something is allowed unless a rule or card text forbids it or a cost can't be paid. "No rule explicitly permits it" is not a reason to answer No.
- To judge a statement true or false, first decide whether the statement as written, including any "not" or "may not", is true; pick Yes only if it is true. State that conclusion in one line just before your final answer line.
- Only a cost (text before a colon, or "pay ...") can stop an effect from being used. Effect text that can't fully happen resolves as much as possible (2.4, 10.10). "You may" parts are optional.
- Numbered sub-steps of a rule happen in their numbered order.
- When two retrieved rules seem to conflict, the more specific one wins, and card text beats the rules (2.5). Check every preloaded rule before answering, not only the first.
- If the preloaded rules don't settle it, call search_rules or get_rule before answering.

Question: It is your rival's turn. Their Delamain Cab is attacking your Emergency Atlus, and you are in the React Step of that attack. You have Field Operator in your hand, a Unit that lacks [QUICK]; it costs 3 €$. To pay costs, you have 1 Eddie ready in your Eddies area and 0 Legends ready in your Legends area. You may pay for Field Operator and play it from your hand now.

Choices:
A. Yes
B. No

Explain your reasoning briefly, citing the rules and cards you used. Then end with one final line of exactly this form:
Answer: <letter>
where <letter> is one of A, B.

2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
2.6. If an effect on a card allows or requires you to do something but another effect prevents it, the preventing effect always takes precedence.

2.8. When cards or effects specify “up to,” you can choose none or 0 (unless there’s a specified minimum).

2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
